collection.title: Time at Home for Whom? Unequal Returns of Paid Family Leave for Infant White Matter and Language Development
collection.authors: Lazarus, M. F.; Nelson, C. A.
collection.abstract: Paid family leave (PFL) may give parents more time with infants, ease financial strain, and support stable routines. Although PFL has been linked to child development, little is known about neural pathways that might underpin its benefits or whether associations vary across families. Using data from 274 infants in the HEALthy Brain and Child Development Study, we examined associations of maternal and paternal PFL with language ability at 12 months and white matter microstructure at 6 months. We tested whether associations varied by the corresponding parent's education. Neither maternal nor paternal PFL was directly associated with language scores or fractional anisotropy in the left arcuate, inferior longitudinal, or uncinate fasciculus. Maternal education moderated associations between maternal PFL and fractional anisotropy in the arcuate (p = .014) and inferior longitudinal fasciculus (p = .003; n = 148). In both tracts, PFL was associated with higher fractional anisotropy only among infants whose mothers had relatively high education. No comparable pattern emerged for language, the uncinate fasciculus, or paternal PFL. Findings suggest that the neurodevelopmental correlates of PFL may depend on family resources rather than operate uniformly across families, underscoring the need to pair paid leave with additional supports and resources.

collection.title: Neurobiological alterations and autism-like phenotype in mice following regulatory-limit exposure to fungicides in drinking water
collection.authors: Salvador-Prince, L.; Vignon, A.; Alenda, U. G.; Lafon, P. A.; Thobois, D.; Schneider, B.; Lehmann, S.; Crozet, C.; Torrent i Mas, J.; Chaloin, L.; Vignes, M.; Laboute, T.; BECKER, J. A. J.; Le Merrer, J.; LOULIER, K.; Perrier, V.
collection.abstract: Neurodevelopmental conditions, including attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorders (ASD), have increased markedly over recent decades. This rise parallels the widespread use of agrochemicals, suggesting a contribution of environmental exposures. We hypothesize that pesticide residues may disrupt brain development and promote neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we test whether concentrations permitted in drinking water affect brain development using a maternal exposure model in wild-type mice. Exposure to a fungicide mixture at 0.3 g/L, below the current European regulatory limit of 0.5 g/L, impairs corticogenesis and is associated with alterations in synaptic function and glutamatergic signaling. Offspring exhibit delays in sensory development, reduced social interactions, and increased stereotyped behaviors. We identify the adenosine A2A receptor as a molecular target of anilinopyrimidine fungicides. Together, these findings indicate that low-dose exposure to this fungicide mixture can induce an autism spectrum-like phenotype in the offspring.

collection.title: Cross Study Regulator Activity Analysis Reveals Convergent Programs in alpha Synuclein PFF Models of Parkinson Disease
collection.authors: Tang, Y.; Xiao, A.; Xiao, Y.; Li, R.; Huang, Z.; Wang, A.; li, L.; Khan, M. M.
collection.abstract: Alpha-synuclein preformed fibril (PFF) models reproduce features of Parkinson disease (PD), but differences in brain region, cell composition, and experimental design complicate comparisons across studies. We reconstructed study-specific regulatory networks using ARACNe (Algorithm for the Reconstruction of Accurate Cellular Networks) and inferred transcription factor (TF) and transcription cofactor activity using VIPER (Virtual Inference of Protein-activity by Enriched Regulon analysis). Five transcriptomic comparisons from four mouse PFF datasets were analyzed, with human PD single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data used to assess cross-species agreement. In the dopamine-neuron-enriched dataset GSE252967, PFF exposure was associated with increased activity of stress- and inflammation-related TFs, including JUND and RELA, and decreased activity of dopaminergic-identity regulators, including NR4A2, LMX1B, FOXA1, FOXA2, PITX3, and EN1. Several regulators were connected to Th in the inferred network. The substantia nigra bulk dataset GSE296779 showed reduced activity of ATF4- and XBP1-associated protein homeostasis and unfolded protein response programs, supported by regulon-weighted gene-set enrichment. Supporting mouse comparisons showed limited overlap in individual TFs but identified changes in inflammatory, glial, and stress-related programs. Agreement between inferred activity and transcript-level changes ranged from 64% to 100% in these comparisons. Human PD data showed cell-type-dependent agreement with mouse findings. EN1 and PITX3 were shared between the mouse and human networks upstream of Th/TH and showed reduced inferred activity in all seven human cell types, alongside nonsignificant decreases in the mouse dataset. These analyses identified changes in dopaminergic-identity, protein homeostasis, and inflammatory transcriptional programs across mouse PFF models, with partial support in human PD.

collection.title: Tasting from memory: reconstructing taste from visual cues in the human brain
collection.authors: Berman, S.; Lawen, A.; Xu, S.; Kahn, I.; Shohamy, D.
collection.abstract: Taste guides us toward nourishment and away from harm. Yet when we decide what to eat, taste only exists in memory, evoked by a cue. How the brain retrieves taste memories is almost entirely unknown. If memory re-creates experience, it should reproduce the brain's activation while tasting, even in the absence of taste. We scanned participants while they formed and then retrieved associations between tastes and visual cues. The gustatory cortex was engaged during retrieval and distinguished among remembered tastes, but not using the patterns it had formed while tasting. Patterns persisted instead in lateral parietal cortex, distinguishing individual tastes, not just taste-categories. Activity in the amygdala covaried with this same parietal region and amygdala activity predicted which associations were retained. Taste memory is not simply a re-creation of sensory experience, but a distinct representation, outside the taste system, yet specific enough to guide what we choose to eat.

collection.title: A novel behavioral paradigm to model hypermemory-like features in rats
collection.authors: Conforti, E.; Chiacchierini, G.; Marchetti, A.; Lisiola, J. M.; Santangelo, V.; Campolongo, P.
collection.abstract: Episodic memory is essential to everyday life and personal identity. However, its dysfunctions can profoundly affect mental health, and translational methods for investigating them in animals remain limited. Most rodent paradigms focus on memory deficits, whereas few tools model abnormally enhanced and persistent memories. Here, we developed a behavioral paradigm to induce hypermemory-like features in adult male and female rats using a version of object recognition (OR) and object location (OL) tasks specifically modified to mimic the rumination-like component of hypermemory. During the odor-context association training, rats explored two identical objects in the presence of a cinnamon scent. Over the following 6 h, they received 12 brief re-exposures in their home cage to either the cinnamon odor or an odor-free stimulus. By repeatedly reactivating the memory trace, these re-exposures promoted its hyperconsolidation without re-exposing animals to the original context or objects. Twenty-four hours later, memory was assessed under odor-free conditions. Odor re-exposure selectively enhanced OL memory in rats of both sexes, whereas OR memory remained unaffected. The procedure did not alter total object exploration or locomotor activity. Enhanced spatial memory was also accompanied by increased c-Fos expression in the ventral hippocampus in both sexes. Our protocol recapitulates key features observed in individuals with hyperfunctional episodic memory: continuous memory reactivation and rumination which may contribute to the excessive strengthening and persistence of specific memories. This simple and reproducible paradigm provides a novel translational tool for investigating the behavioral and neurobiological mechanisms underlying memory hyperconsolidation and maladaptive memory persistence.

collection.title: Precision cell-state silencing of injured afferents alleviates spontaneous neuropathic pain
collection.authors: Cooper, A. H.; Chrysostomidou, P.; Jurado Santos, A.; Cui, H.; Adesida, S.; Redondo Canales, M.; Bakina, A.; Barry, A. M.; Baskozos, G.; Bennett, D. L.; Weir, G. A.
collection.abstract: Excessive primary afferent activity sustains neuropathic pain, but safe and effective therapeutic inhibition has proved elusive. Realising the promise of gene therapies to meet this challenge requires strategies to identify and selectively target the neuronal populations responsible. Here, we use chemo- and optogenetic approaches to demonstrate that activity in injured afferents drives spontaneous pain but is dispensable for normal sensory function, thereby creating a therapeutic opportunity. Guided by chromatin accessibility profiling, we create an injury-responsive viral vector that confers >95% specificity for injured sensory neurons. Combined with the translationally relevant chemogenetic PSAM4-GlyR, this targeting module effectively silences hyperexcitable human sensory neurons and alleviates spontaneous neuropathic pain in mice. These findings establish precision cell-state targeting of sensory neurons as a promising therapeutic strategy for chronic pain.

collection.title: Agency and Embodiment Provide Dissociable Benefits to Perception, Metacognition and Neural Processing During Active Sensing
collection.authors: Tang, Z.; Dowsett, J.; Taylor, P.; Ferreiro, D. N.; Pecka, M.
collection.abstract: Metacognition, judging how reliable our own perceptual decisions are, is central to adaptive behavior. Such judgments hinge on the reliability of the sensory evidence on which that decision is based, and active sensing through self-directed exploration is known to improve perception itself. Yet, how agency, the authorship over self-initiated actions, and the processing of the sensory consequences, which is implicit to active sensing, modulate metacognition and its calibration, remains unknown. Whether physical embodiment adds to this beyond virtual exploration is similarly unclear, yet relevant both for daily life and for self-monitoring in agentic AI. Here, we combined a naturalistic auditory search paradigm with mobile electroencephalography. Twenty participants performed a target-detection task under three conditions: active embodied exploration , active screen-based exploration, and passive listening to replays of their own trials, while we obtained steady-state auditory evoked potentials (SSAEPs) to characterize stimulus-locked neural responses. We find that both agency conditions improved accuracy, metacognitive sensitivity, and overall SSAEP amplitude relative to passive listening, indicating that agency, rather than whole-body movement, drives these enhancements. Crucially, however, embodiment uniquely grounded both the target-evoked neural response and the subjects' confidence to immediate sensory evidence. Thus, agency alone broadly enhances perceptual and neural processing, but embodiment specifically anchors confidence, neurally and behaviorally, to the present.

collection.title: Early-life vancomycin and meropenem treatment exert distinct effects on microbiota-gut-brain axis signalling in zebrafish larvae
collection.authors: Faimann, I.; Ghosh, A.; Tatzl, E.; Stojanovic, N.; Penker, R.; Rodriguez-Blanco, G.; Reichmann, F.
collection.abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis is a bidirectional communication pathway between the gastrointestinal tract, gut microbiota and the central nervous system, that influences host neurobiology, metabolism and behaviour. Although germ-free and antibiotic-treated animals demonstrate a role for microbial signalling in mood and behaviour, mechanisms linking microbiome disruption to altered neural signalling during early development remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the impact of antibiotic-induced perturbations of the gut microbiota on behaviour, neurotransmitter levels as well as central and peripheral metabolism in 5 dpf zebrafish larvae, an established neurodevelopmental model. Larvae were exposed to the broad-spectrum antibiotic meropenem, the Gram-positive-directed antibiotic vancomycin, or their combination, and assessed gut microbiota composition, behaviour, neurotransmitter levels and metabolite profiles. All treatments altered microbial community composition, although the extent differed markedly, with pronounced restructuring after meropenem and combination treatment and more subtle changes after vancomycin. Behavioural analysis using the light-dark transition assay revealed reduced centre locomotion during the dark phase in all treated groups, without a general reduction in swimming activity, consistent with anxiety-like behaviour. These behavioural changes were accompanied by reduced expression of serotonergic genes and widespread central and peripheral metabolic disruptions in all antibiotic-treated groups. Treatment- and tissue-specific effects included suppression of the arginine-polyamine pathway in the brain following vancomycin treatment and increased peripheral glutamate, GABA and L-DOPA levels after meropenem exposure. collection.title: Coupled neuro-fluid dynamics in human bioelectromagnetism
collection.authors: Popov, T.; Miller, G. A.
collection.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) are widely interpreted as direct, non-invasive measures of neural population activity, assuming surrounding tissue and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) act as passive volume conductors that distorts but do not contribute to signal generation. Using conductive-fluid phantom experiments, structural magnetic resonance imaging, and in vivo EEG and MEG recordings, the present report challenges this assumption. Mechanically driven conductive fluid generated structured, oscillatory, source-localizable electromagnetic signals resembling M/EEG in the absence of neural tissue, and interindividual differences in CSF volume systematically moderated M/EEG signal amplitude. These findings suggest that, at the scales accessed by invasive and non-invasive electrophysiology, electromagnetic and mechanical processes form a coupled system in which contributions of neural currents and fluid motion cannot readily be uniquely separated.

collection.title: Dynamic interactions between sensory and decision-making circuits shape temporal evidence weighting
collection.authors: Vivar, C.; Ferro, D.; Levi, A. J.; Huk, A. C.; Wimmer, K.
collection.abstract: Perceptual decisions require the brain to integrate sensory evidence over time, yet the temporal weighting of evidence can be flexibly adjusted according to task demands. How such flexibility emerges from interactions between sensory and decision circuits remains unclear. Here, we combined behavioral and neural measurements with recurrent network modeling to investigate the mechanisms underlying temporal weighting of sensory evidence. Macaques performed a motion-discrimination task in which the temporal statistics of sensory evidence favored early, late or uniform integration. Behavioral psychophysical kernels revealed corresponding shifts in the influence of evidence across time, accompanied by systematic changes in motion discriminability and choice-related activity modulation in visual area MT. We developed a recurrent sensory-decision network incorporating reciprocal feedforward and feedback interactions and a temporally structured modulatory input, resembling an urgency signal. The model reproduced the observed behavioral and neural signatures across temporal weighting conditions. Mechanistically, shifting the onset and dynamics of modulatory inputs systematically reconfigured the temporal profile of evidence weighting without substantially altering sensory response dynamics. Choice-related activity in MT can be decomposed in a bottom-up component with the same time-course as the psychophysical kernel, and a top-down component reflecting the decision build-up. These findings suggest that flexible temporal integration can emerge from dynamic interactions between sensory transmission, recurrent decision circuits and temporally structured urgency modulation, providing a mechanistic framework for how neural systems adapt the computation of sensory evidence to changing task demands.

collection.title: Psychopharmacological Effects of Cannabidiol in Rodent Models of Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review of Behavioral Outcomes, Neurobiological Mechanisms, and Methodological Quality
collection.authors: Domingues, B. R. R.; Felix, G. S.; Bezerra, M. F. L.; Medeiros, P.; de Freitas, R. L.
collection.abstract: ABSTRACT Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interaction, as well as restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior. Although increasing evidence suggests that cannabidiol (CBD) may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for ASD, the preclinical literature remains fragmented, with substantial variability in experimental models, treatment protocols, CBD formulations, and reported outcomes. This systematic review (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251177933) aimed to critically evaluate the psychopharmacological effects of CBD in rodent models of ASD, with an emphasis on behavioral outcomes, underlying neurobiological mechanisms, and methodological quality. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses, with a final sample of 14 articles. Due to the substantial heterogeneity across studies, a qualitative synthesis of results was performed using the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) approach. Overall, CBD and CBD-based preparations produced beneficial effects across multiple ASD-relevant behavioral domains. Enhanced social interaction, reductions in repetitive behaviors, anxiety-like responses, and cognitive impairments were observed in specific models. Neurobiological analyses revealed modulation of the endocannabinoid system, restoration of excitation/inhibition balance, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, and transcriptional regulation. Positive outcomes were observed across pharmacological, genetic, and maternal immune activation models, suggesting that CBD acts on convergent neurobiological pathways implicated in ASD pathophysiology. collection.title: Midbrain somatostatin-expressing cells control pain-suppression during defensive states
collection.authors: Winke, N.; Aby, F.; Jercog, D.; Riffault, C.; Bouali-Benazzouz, R.; Viellard, J.; Girard, D.; Grivet, Z.; Landry, M.; Castell, L.; Valjent, E.; Valerio, S.; Fossat, P.; Herry, C.
collection.abstract: In threatening situations, animals exhibit a broad range of behavioral and autonomic responses. As such, a crucial adaptive response is the inhibition of pain, which facilitates relevant defensive behaviors that promote survival. Whereas the structures and mechanisms involved in fear and pain behaviors are well documented, little is known about the precise neuronal mechanisms mediating the emotional regulation of endogenous pain-suppression. Here, we used a combination of behavioral, anatomical, optogenetic, and electrophysiological approaches to investigate, in male mice, the role of somatostatin-expressing cells in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (SST+ vlPAG cells) in the control of analgesia induced during defensive states. Our data indicate that optogenetic inhibition of SST+ vlPAG cells promotes analgesia irrespective of animal defensive state. In contrast, optogenetic activation of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells that project to the rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM) abolishes the analgesia mediated by fear behavior. Together, these results identify a novel circuit mechanism composed of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells projecting to the RVM that regulate analgesia elicited during defensive states.
